mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a month is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during such rate spikes (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not spike above 5.25% in any observed month.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer payrolls (GDPC1) signals weakening labor market strength, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while GDPC1 decreases in the same month
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 60-day forward returns are positive when this dual signal persists (p < 0.05), or the interaction rank IC exceeds 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,600K accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests an imbalance favoring demand, predicting positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day returns when this pattern occurs (p > 0.05), or the interaction is not statistically significant (rank IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for two consecutive months predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns due to supply-side contraction.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 60-day forward returns are not negative when INDPRO declines for two consecutive months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months during a monetary easing regime, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5 for three consecutive months and regime_hint is 'easing'
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when the trigger occurs (p > 0.05), or UNRATE does not fall below 3.5 for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 jobs without a corresponding increase in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests labor market over-heating and predicts negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 in a single month while INDPRO remains flat or declines
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when this pattern occurs (p > 0.05), or interaction rank IC exceeds 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of 0.5% or more for three consecutive months is associated with negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns due to deflationary expectations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by 0.5% or more each month for three months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative when CPIAUCSL declines by 1.5% over three months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the 10-year yield proxy (FEDFUNDS) below 2.5% for 10 consecutive months predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as lower discounting boosts present-value pricing.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when FEDFUNDS remains below 2.5% for 10 consecutive months (p > 0.05).
